speaker: Patient
text: Physical examination shows epicanthus, upward slanting of the eyelids, low-set ears, and a single transverse palmar crease. A grade 2/6 holosystolic murmur heard at the left mid to lower sternal border. The lungs are clear to auscultation. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Diaphragmatic Hernia (Bochdalek hernia) associated with Trisomy 21 (Down Syndrome).

The physical exam findings of epicanthus, upward slanting eyelids, low-set ears, and a single transverse palmar crease are classic for Down syndrome. The holosystolic murmur likely represents a concurrent congenital heart defect (such as a VSD), which is common in this population. The presenting symptoms of feeding intolerance and bilious vomiting in a newborn are highly suggestive of a lower gastrointestinal obstruction, such as a volvulus or, given the urgency, a hernia with incarceration. The combination of a cardiac defect, dysmorphic features, and acute GI obstruction in a newborn strongly points to a complex congenital anomaly requiring immediate surgical evaluation.
